title: Somatic mosaicism in the brain: linking development, ageing and neurodegeneration
title_zh: 大脑体细胞 mosaicism：连接发育、衰老与神经退行性疾病
abstract: Somatic mosaicism is increasingly recognized as a pervasive feature of the human brain and a potential contributor to neurological disease across the lifespan. Unlike germline variants, somatic variants arise post-zygotically and are unevenly distributed across regions, cell types and even individual neurons, enabling focal biological effects that can scale to network-level dysfunction. In this Review, we synthesize current evidence that developmental timing, clonal architecture and cell-type-specific selective pressures shape how somatic variants influence brain structure and function. Early embryonic variants can produce broad regional clones and severe phenotypes, whereas later events are usually more restricted; with ageing, ongoing DNA damage and imperfect repair generate private variants that might cumulatively reduce cellular resilience. We also summarize advances in detection approaches, including bulk, error-corrected and single-cell sequencing, and discuss their strengths and current limitations for clinical translation. Emerging data link brain somatic variants to neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative phenotypes, supporting a unified framework in which mosaic genetics bridges focal lesions and distributed neurological syndromes. Integrating genomic, cellular and physiological analyses in longitudinal human studies will be essential to define causality, identify biomarkers and guide future targeted interventions. Somatic mosaicism is now recognized as widespread in the human brain and a potential contributor to neurological disease across the lifespan. This Review outlines how developmental timing, clonal structure and cell-type pressures shape variant effects and summarizes advances and limitations in detection methods.
abstract_zh: 体细胞 mosaicism 越来越被认可为人类大脑中普遍存在的特征，并可能在整个生命周期中导致神经系统疾病。与胚系变异不同，体细胞变异在受精后产生，并在脑区、细胞类型甚至单个神经元之间不均匀分布，这种局部生物学效应可扩展至网络级功能障碍。在本综述中，我们综合了当前证据，阐明发育时间点、克隆架构和细胞类型特异性选择压力如何影响体细胞变异对大脑结构和功能的影响。早期胚胎变异可产生广泛区域克隆和严重表型，而后期事件通常更为局限；随着年龄增长，持续的 DNA 损伤和不完美的修复会产生私人变异，这些变异可能累积降低细胞韧性。我们还概括了检测方法的进展，包括 bulk、错配校正和单细胞测序，并讨论了其优势和当前局限性，以便临床转化。新兴数据将大脑体细胞变异与神经发育和神经退行性表型联系起来，支持一个统一框架，即马赛克遗传学在聚焦病变和分布式神经系统综合征之间搭桥。在纵向人体研究中整合基因组学、细胞学和生理分析对于定义因果关系、识别生物标志物和指导未来的靶向干预至关重要。体细胞 mosaicism 现在被广泛认可为人类大脑中的常见现象，并可能是全生命周期神经系统疾病的潜在促成因素。本综述概述了发育时间点、克隆结构和细胞类型压力如何影响变异效应，并总结了检测方法的进展与局限性。
